extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was manually collected by a team of over 50 college students (including co-authors) from various disciplines, who gathered multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Secondary Data analysis; Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, major textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students specializing in relevant majors collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise. Annotators adhered to copyright regulations and selected questions without immediately available answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicates identified via lexical overlap and URL similarity were reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, and authors categorized the problems into four difficulty levels. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors
